points: Basic repro: `@SuperBuilder class ChildWithAnnotation extends Parent<@ValidDouble Double>` (Parent<T extends Comparable<T>> with @SuperBuilder) → delombok output has `extends Parent.ParentBuilder<@ValidDouble Double, C, B>` (3 type args, Double kept) and compiles without the 'wrong number of type arguments' error; the ecj output also matches

Multiple type arguments where only some are annotated, e.g. `Parent<@A String, Integer>` or `Parent<@A String, @B Integer>` → the generated builder's extends clause keeps all superclass arguments in order, followed by C and B (argument count = superclass type parameter count + 2)

Annotation with parameters on the type argument, e.g. `Parent<@TA(x=5) Double>` → the argument is not dropped and the generated code compiles; the annotation is either kept intact or consistently stripped, matching the after-delombok file
Nested generic argument containing an annotation, e.g. `Parent<List<@A String>>` → the builder's superclass arguments are preserved and generated correctly

Fully qualified annotated type argument, e.g. `Parent<java.lang.@A Double>`, or wildcard/array type arguments (`Parent<? extends Number>`, `Parent<@A String[]>`) → none are silently dropped from the generated ParentBuilder<...> argument list

Regression: un-annotated `Child extends Parent<Double>` and the existing SuperBuilderWithGenerics* cases → output stays unchanged (`ParentBuilder<Double, C, B>`); the builder() and build() methods of the annotated child also work with the annotated generic parent, with the type argument carried through to the type of the value field
